facts.text: In Norse myth Fjalar and Galar are the dwarves who murdered Kvasir and brewed the mead of poetry from his blood.
The two in Skona taking those names is Living Server lore (zone_skona topic 'Fjalar and Galar').

story:
Fjalar and his brother Galar wander the west of Skona together under the names of the two dwarves of the old tale, who murdered Kvasir, the wisest of men, and brewed the mead of poetry from his blood, and drowned a giant and his wife for good measure. They do not deny it. The Seithkona Circle will not have them near. Fjalar is the elder and does the talking, and what he talks about, Gudny says, is the mead: where it went when Odin stole it, whether there is any left, and whether a man who drank a little of it would be able to say things that cannot be unsaid.

The Circle thinks they are only two dwarves with ugly names and a taste for trouble who came north from the dverge forges. The skalds of Galplen think they are the dwarves of the tale, still looking for the mead. Either way the brothers fight together and fall together, and Fjalar has never once been seen without Galar a step behind him. The green orm by the river avoids them.
legend: Fjalar (37) and Galar (36) are two dwarves who stand together in the west of Skona near the river. Pull one and you get both, every time; no faction, no spells, just two hitters. Kill Galar first if you want the shorter fight, the old players say, since Fjalar talks. They stand in the open by the river, so you can see them coming; there's a green orm nearby that you don't want to drag in by accident.

aggro: The mead! Have you tasted it? No? Then you're of no use to me.

lairEntry: Two dwarves by the river, arguing about mead.
